explicit_summary_lines: Every Standard Tasks button checks the ChatGPT chat binding before its input dialog, its question or the Kit's release request: a chat of another repository is named at once with the step that resolves it, no longer after the owner confirmed; the start still checks it again, and a regression test guards the order (AGP_CHAT_BINDING_BEFORE_CONFIRM_V1); build `release-0.3.6-r4`.

Kit 1.1.10 adopted through the standard task „Kit übernehmen“ and the Kit's own `kit update` (manifest c75ff9f747e1, signature 74c7e1dd132720bc096ba736, #418); CI pins, entrypoints, command reference and rule inventory follow 1.1.10.

Kit findings register follows Kit 1.1.10 (retest PASS 52, FAIL 0, evidence docs/validation/evidence/kit-1.1.10-adoption.json): KIT-GF-093, the release check of an editable install, is verified fixed; no Kit finding is open.

„Kit übernehmen“ (Standard Tasks → „Weitere anzeigen“) asks the Kit whether a newer stable Kit release exists. Nothing to adopt — current, ahead, an editable checkout or not checkable — shows an information window and starts nothing. A newer release confirms the exact version and starts a task that adopts it through the Kit's own update route on `chore/kit-<version>`; the signed execute of the update is always the owner's decision (`kit update` joins the owner-decision executes), the changes stay on the branch for „Abschließen“ and a local verifier checks branch, installed Kit and CI pins (AGP_KIT_ADOPT_TASK_V1); build `release-0.3.6-r3`.

The Systemcheck shows a line „Kit-Release“ with the Kit's own answer to whether a newer stable Kit release exists (`kit status --check-release`, Kit 1.1.9): current, newer available with the step that adopts it, ahead, or not checkable; for an editable install whose reported version differs from the running one it shows the contradiction instead of advice (KIT-GF-093) (AGP_KIT_RELEASE_CHECK_V1); build `release-0.3.6-r2`.
Kit 1.1.9 adopted through the Kit's own `kit update` (manifest 357a6861eea4, signature b176f82eba913d224b1d2ab5); CI pins, entrypoints, command reference and rule inventory follow 1.1.9.
